title: Vue binding
description:
How one agnostic component contract is realised in Vue. The reasoning is in packages/contracts/README.md.

Everything here is a fact that stops being true the moment you build the same contract on a different framework. It is deliberately SMALLER than the React binding, and the two fields it does not have are the finding: Vue merges a consumer's `class` onto the root element by itself, and exposes that element as `$el`, so `classNamePassthrough` and `refTarget` have nothing to record. React needs both stated because React supplies neither.

Keep it SMALL. If a field here would be equally true in React, it belongs in `@ds/platform-web` or in the contract instead.

component.description: Must match the contract's `component`, the directory name, and the name of the emitted <Name>.vue single-file component.

contract.description: Relative path to the agnostic contract this realises.

framework.description: Named explicitly so a directory can hold more than one binding without ambiguity.

element.description:
The element rendered at the root — what the contract's `semantics.role` becomes in the DOM.

IDENTICAL to the React binding's `element` in all fifteen components, and that is a measurement rather than a coincidence: which element carries a role is web-platform knowledge, not framework knowledge. It is duplicated here deliberately and the duplication is reported in docs/research/0004 rather than removed, because removing it before it was measured would have been a guess.

elementByProp.description: For polymorphic components. Vue's own idiom is `<component :is>`; this records the same fact the React binding records, and the emitter spells it Vue's way.

map.description: Prop value, or `present`/`absent` for a boolean, -> rendered element.

exposes.description:
Anatomy nodes published through `defineExpose` beyond the root.

The ROOT is never listed: Vue exposes a single-root component's element as `$el` with no help from the emitter, which is why this field has no `refTarget` equivalent. It exists for the case a consumer must reach a node further in — and nothing needs it yet, so every binding omits it. An empty field that is honest about being unexercised beats a field invented to mirror React's.

propOverrides.description: Where a contract axis is exposed under a different prop name in Vue, because the framework already owns the canonical one. Keyed by axis name.

reason.description: Required. A rename with no reason is drift with paperwork.
